units.title: Sequence and Series
units.intro: A **sequence** is a list $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$. A **series** is the sum $S_n=a_1+\cdots+a_n$.

cards.title: 1.1 Basic Ideas of Sequence
body: For each of the sequences in task (3) try to find a general formula that describes the given sequence.
A sequence in mathematics is a function whose domain is the set of positive integers.
If the domain consists of the first “n” positive integers only, then the sequence is a finite sequence.
Remark: The general formula of a sequence is also known as the nth term formula of the sequence.
For n a natural number n, nfactorial, denoted by n! is the product of the first n natural numbers.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Find the $$7^{\text{th}}$$ term of the sequence given by $$a_n = (-1)^n(2n + 3)$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the given values**
We need to find the term for $$n = 7$$ in the formula $$a_n = (-1)^n(2n + 3)$$.

**Step 2: Substitute $$n = 7$$**
$$a_7 = (-1)^7(2(7) + 3)$$

**Step 3: Compute the expression**
$$a_7 = (-1) \times (14 + 3)$$
$$a_7 = -17$$

**Step 4: Final Result**
The seventh term is **$$-17$$**.

cards.title: Arithmetic (AP)
body: Common difference $d=a_{k+1}-a_k$ (constant).
$$a_n=a_1+(n-1)d\qquad S_n=\frac{n}{2}\bigl(2a_1+(n-1)d\bigr)=\frac{n}{2}(a_1+a_n)$$

cards.title: Trick
body: If you know first and last, use $S_n=\frac{n}{2}(a_1+a_n)$ — fewer slips than the $2a_1$ form. To find $n$, solve $a_n=a_1+(n-1)d$ for $n$ and check it is a whole number.

cards.title: Geometric (GP)
body: Common ratio $r=a_{k+1}/a_k$ (constant, $r\neq0$).
$$a_n=a_1 r^{n-1}\qquad S_n=a_1\frac{r^n-1}{r-1}\ (r\neq1)\qquad |r|<1:\ S_\infty=\frac{a_1}{1-r}$$

cards.title: Trick
body: Write the ratio as a fraction, not a rounded decimal, until the last line. For $S_\infty$ first ask: is $|r|<1$? If $|r|\ge 1$ there is no finite infinite sum.

questions.q: The Arithmetic mean and Harmonic mean between two numbers are 27 and 12, respectively. Find their Geometric mean.
why: For positive a, b: AM = (a + b)/2, GM = √(ab), HM = 2ab/(a + b), so AM × HM = ab = GM².
GM² = 27 × 12 = 324 → GM = 18. (The numbers are 9 and 45.) Answer: B.

The values 'Healthy', 'Mildly Ill', and 'Severely Ill' describe non-numerical attributes or characteristics of the students.

**Step 2: Compare with statistical definitions**
Variables that allow for classification based on attributes are qualitative (or categorical) variables. Quantitative variables must represent numerical counts or measurements.

cards.title: 2.2 Organizing Data
body: Variable is the characteristic of interest of an element that can assume different values for the different elements in the population or sample.
Datum: The values that a variable can assume are called data (single measured value (singular of data)) Data or Data Set: collection of numerical / non-numerical values (plural of datum).
Data are facts or figures from which conclusions can be drawn.
Qualitative (or categorical) variables allow for classification of individuals based on some attribute or characteristic.
Quantitative variable represents a counted or measured quantity.

cards.title: 2.3 Statistical graphs
body: A pie chart is a circle divided into sectors.
The area of each sector is proportional to the frequency of the category.
A bar graph is constructed by labelling each category of data on a horizontal axis and the frequency or relative frequency of the category on the vertical axis.
Rectangles of equal width are drawn for each category.
The height of each rectangle is the category’s frequency or relative frequency.

cards.title: 2.4 Statistical Analysis of Ungrouped Data
body: The test had five questions, each carrying ten marks.
A measure of central tendency is a single value that can be used to represent all the other values in the collection.
The median divides the array into two equal parts.

If the number of observations is even, the median is simply the middle observation in the array while if the number of observations is odd, the median is the average of the two middle observations in the array.
The median of a variable is the value that lies in the middle of the data when arranged in ascending order.

cards.title: Averages
body: Raw data mean $\bar x=\dfrac{\sum x}{n}$. Grouped: $\bar x=\dfrac{\sum f x}{\sum f}$ (use class midpoints as $x$).
Median: middle value when ordered (or $L+\dfrac{\frac{n}{2}-F}{f}\times c$ for grouped). Mode: most frequent class.

cards.title: Trick — which average?
body: Mean uses every number (sensitive to outliers). Median is the “typical middle”. Mode is the fashion — useful for sizes/shoes. If the question says “average” with no adjective, they usually want the mean.

cards.title: Spread
body: Range $= \max-\min$. Variance uses squared deviations; standard deviation $\sigma$ is the square root (same units as the data). Larger $\sigma$ → more spread.

cards.title: 2.5 Probability
body: In statistics, the word experiment is used to describe any process that generates a set of data.
A phenomenon is called random if individual outcomes are uncertain but there is nonetheless a regular distribution of outcomes in a large number of repetitions.
Any process which generates well defined outcomes is called an experiment.
The number of trials is the total number of times the experiment is repeated.
The outcomes are the different results possible for one trial of the experiment.

Complement: $P(A')=1-P(A)$. If $A$ and $B$ cannot happen together (mutually exclusive), $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$. If independent, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$.

cards.q: Calculate the distance between the two endpoints of a line segment given as $$A(3, 2)$$ and $$B(13, 10)$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: State the distance formula**
The distance between two points $$(x_1, y_1)$$ and $$(x_2, y_2)$$ is:
$$d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$$

**Step 2: Substitute the coordinates**
Here, $$A(3, 2)$$ and $$B(13, 10)$$ are given. Substitute these coordinates:
$$d = \sqrt{(13 - 3)^2 + (10 - 2)^2}$$

**Step 3: Simplify the terms**
$$d = \sqrt{(10)^2 + (8)^2}$$
$$d = \sqrt{100 + 64}$$

$$M = \left( \frac{3 + 13}{2}, \frac{2 + 10}{2} \right)$$

**Step 3: Perform the calculations**
$$M = \left( \frac{16}{2}, \frac{12}{2} \right)$$
$$M = (8, 6)$$

Slope $m=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$. Line: $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$ or $y=mx+c$. Parallel ⇒ same $m$. Perpendicular ⇒ $m_1 m_2=-1$.

body: A circle is the set of all points in a plane that are equidistant from a fixed point.

cards.title: 4.1 Operations on Matrices
body: A matrix is an ordered rectangular array of numbers.
The numbers are called the elements or the entries of the matrix.
A matrix in which the number of rows is equal to the number of columns is called a square matrix.
A square matrix in which elements in the diagonal are all 1 and rest are all zeros is called an identity matrix.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the order of the following matrix: $$A = \begin{pmatrix} -2 & 2 \\ 5 & 9 \end{pmatrix}$$?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Count the number of rows**
The horizontal lines of elements are the rows. Matrix $$A$$ has $$2$$ rows.

**Step 2: Count the number of columns**
The vertical lines of elements are the columns. Matrix $$A$$ has $$2$$ columns.

**Step 3: State the order**
The order is given as $$m \times n$$ where $$m$$ is rows and $$n$$ is columns. Therefore, the order is $$2 \times 2$$.

**Step 4: Final R

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If $$\begin{pmatrix} x+2 & 5 \\ 1 & y-3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$$, find the values of $$x$$ and $$y$$.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Understand matrix equality**
Two matrices are equal if and only if their corresponding elements are equal.

**Step 2: Set up equations for the variables**
From the entry in row 1, column 1:
$$x + 2 = 7 \implies x = 7 - 2 = 5$$

From the entry in row 2, column 2:
$$y - 3 = 2 \implies y = 2 + 3 = 5$$

**Step 3: Final Result**
The values are **$$x = 5, y = 5$$**.

body: $$\begin{vmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{vmatrix}=ad-bc$$
If $\det A\neq 0$, $A$ is invertible. Cramer’s rule / inverse method solves $AX=B$.

cards.title: Tricks
body: Matrix multiplication is *not* commutative: $AB$ may exist when $BA$ does not. For $2\times 2$ inverse: swap $a$ and $d$, change signs of $b$ and $c$, divide by $ad-bc$. If determinant is $0$, stop — no unique inverse.
